mxmlNewTextf: Takes the string as format_args!.
mxmlLoadFd: Reads any std::io::Read, as a file descriptor was read.

mxmlSetTextf: Takes the string as format_args!.

The whole port is done. The library is now standalone safe Rust (no `unsafe` anywhere), and all 10 planned units are committed on `codecoremorph/20261116-130929-5708`. The final check, a clean build plus the full test run, passed. The run took about 102 minutes and made no model calls.

| Unit | What it ported | Attempts | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-0001 | `mxml-private.c`: default type callbacks, per-thread global data | 1 | `378c319` |
| U-0002 | `mxml-entity.c`: entity callbacks, standard entity table | 1 | `d995dc4` |
| U-0003 | `mxml-attr.c`: attributes | 1 | `9a5cf50` |
| U-0004 | `mxml-get.c`: the 14 getters | 1 | `3053024` |
| U-0005 | `mxml-node.c`: building the tree, deleting, reference counts | 1 | `62b3ff6` |
| U-0006 | `mxml-file.c`: the XML loader and writer | 3 | `b4fbab8` |
| U-0007 | `mxml-search.c`: tree walking, find element, find path | 1 | `63867a6` |
| U-0008 | `mxml-index.c`: indexes | 1 | `c119712` |
| U-0009 | `mxml-set.c`: the setters | 1 | `824b662` |
| U-0010 | Retirement: deleted the C and the Make build | 2 | `fdeb8e5` |

**What changed in the retirement (U-0010):**
- **Node handles:** the API now works on a Rust `Document` holding all the nodes, with node handles in place of C pointers.
- **Callbacks and I/O:** callbacks are Rust functions and closures. Input is any reader or byte string, output any writer or buffer.
- **Variadic functions:** the C's `printf`-style functions (`mxml_error`, the `...f` setters) take `format_args!`.
- **Tests:** the C test program `testmxml.c` was deleted. `rust/mxml_rs/tests/testmxml.rs` (10 tests) takes over the one baseline test, `make test`. It repeats the program's checks and its three output comparisons on `test.xml`, which all passed before the port.
- **Maps:** `rust/symbol-map.toml` maps all 82 C functions to the Rust that replaced them, and `rust/test-map.toml` maps `make:test` to the 10 tests.

**What the verification didn't cover:**
- **No characterization tests were written.** The run flagged 47 untested functions, but the tool can't add such tests to this autoconf build yet. The fix it suggested was a manifest setting, and the manifest is outside the folder I can write to, so I dropped all 10 jobs. Those functions were checked only by the existing test and, at the end, the new Rust tests.
- **Six C++ files aren't built** in this configuration (`test/class.cxx`, `enum.cxx`, `function.cxx`, `functype.cxx`, `struct.cxx`, `type.cxx`). No unit changed them.
- **Other platforms' build files are stale.** `vcnet/` and `xcode/` were excluded from the port and still list the deleted C files.
- **No tests were excused.** Nothing was skipped, too large or left out of the plan. The plan had no units for programs or test files because it found none to port.

**Behavior that differs from the C, all recorded in the report:**
- Several inputs that crashed the C (null strings or file pointers, elements with no name) now get a null result or an error instead.
- Real numbers are parsed and printed in Rust, matching glibc for ordinary values. Hexadecimal float input is only approximated.
- Custom node data is now owned and dropped by Rust instead of freed by a destroy callback, and user data is a plain integer.
- File saves buffer their output and flush at the end.

**Two tool quirks I worked around, both in U-0006:**
- **Interface check:** the check treated a callback type as changed because the header and the C source spell it differently. I kept six redeclarations in `mxml-file.c` until the retirement deleted it.
- **ABI check:** this check only looks at files changed in the current attempt, so a retry that doesn't touch the Rust crate fails it falsely.

To review: `git diff fd47c7d codecoremorph/20261116-130929-5708`, or `git log` on that branch for one commit per unit. Nothing has been merged.

The full report is at `E:\codecoremorph-trials\c-eval\mxml\.codecoremorph\runs\20261116-130929-5708\report.md`.
